skill_tags: Complex Polar Form and De Moivre's Theorem

hints: Apply De Moivre's theorem to the numerator: $\left(\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right)\right)^4 = \cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{7}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{7}\right)$.
Express the denominator in standard polar form with argument $-\dfrac{\pi}{7}$, and use $\arg(z_1/z_2) = \arg z_1 - \arg z_2$.
walkthrough:
Apply De Moivre's theorem to the numerator:
$$\left(\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right)\right)^4 = \cos\left(4 \times \dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(4 \times \dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) = \cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{7}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{7}\right)$$
So $\arg(\text{Numerator}) = \dfrac{4\pi}{7}$.

Rewrite the denominator in standard polar form using $\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta$ and $\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta$:
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) - \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) = \cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right)$$
So $\arg(\text{Denominator}) = -\dfrac{\pi}{7}$.

Subtract the arguments to find the argument of the quotient:
$$\arg u = \arg(\text{Numerator}) - \arg(\text{Denominator}) = \dfrac{4\pi}{7} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right) = \dfrac{4\pi}{7} + \dfrac{\pi}{7} = \dfrac{5\pi}{7}$$

ai_rubric.Complex Polar Form and De Moivre's Theor: States or implies arguments $4\pi/7$ and $-\pi/7$ (M1). Obtains exact argument $\arg u = 5\pi/7$ (A1).

hints: Recall that the complex conjugate $u^*$ reflects $u$ across the real axis.
Use $\arg u^* = -\arg u$ to evaluate the argument.
walkthrough:
Identify the geometrical effect of complex conjugation:
For any complex number $u = x + \mathrm{i}y$, its complex conjugate is $u^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$. The real coordinate remains the same while the imaginary coordinate changes sign.

Describe the single geometrical transformation:
The transformation mapping $u$ onto $u^*$ is a **reflection in the real axis** (or reflection in the $x$-axis).

Determine the argument of $u^*$:
$$\arg u^* = -\arg u = -\dfrac{5\pi}{7}$$

ai_rubric.Complex Algebra: Identifies transformation as reflection in the real axis (B1). States exact argument $\arg u^* = -5\pi/7$ (B1).
